meaning.en: To be slightly better than one's opponent; a notch above.
meaning.zh: 比对手稍微高明一点。

examples.zh: 这场比赛，对手棋高一着，我们输得心服口服。
examples.en: In this match our opponent was a notch better and we lost with good grace.

examples.zh: 论经验，还是他棋高一着。
examples.en: In experience, he still has the edge.

examples.zh: 商场如棋局，谁棋高一着，谁就能赢。
examples.en: Business is like a chess game: whoever is a move ahead wins.

usage.en: Often in the saying 棋高一着，缚手缚脚 or 棋高一着，胜人半筹; 着 here is zhāo (a move). Used of small but decisive superiority.
usage.zh: 常用“棋高一着，缚手缚脚”之说；“着”读zhāo（棋步）。指稍胜一筹。

meaning.en: To die an unnatural or unhappy death; to come to a bad end.
meaning.zh: 不能平安地度过一生，指死于非命或结局很惨。

examples.zh: 作恶多端的人往往不得善终。
examples.en: Evildoers often come to a bad end.

examples.zh: 他得罪了权贵，最后不得善终。
examples.en: He offended the powerful and in the end met a bad end.

examples.zh: 故事里的反派不得善终，大快人心。
examples.en: The villain in the story gets his comeuppance, to everyone's satisfaction.

usage.en: Often a curse-like verdict or moral warning; avoid in polite talk about real people who have died. Predicate.
usage.zh: 带诅咒或劝诫意味；对真实逝者不宜用。作谓语。

natural: five blessings arrive at the door

meaning.en: A New Year wish: may all good fortune come to your household.
meaning.zh: 新年祝福语，希望家中福气齐来。

equivalents: may fortune smile on your house

examples.zh: 祝您新春快乐，五福临门！
examples.en: Happy New Year, and may blessings fill your home!

examples.zh: 门上贴着“五福临门”的剪纸。
examples.en: A paper-cut reading 'Five Blessings at the Door' is pasted on the door.

examples.zh: 春节拜年，他说了句五福临门，老人乐开了花。
examples.en: Paying a New Year call he wished them five blessings, and the old folk beamed.

usage.en: A set greeting, mainly at Spring Festival; the five blessings are usually longevity, wealth, health, virtue and a good end. Often on couplets.
usage.zh: 春节常用祝福语；“五福”常指长寿、富贵、康宁、好德、善终。常见于春联、剪纸。

natural: the sea of learning has no shore

meaning.en: There is no end to knowledge, so one should keep learning.
meaning.zh: 学问像大海一样没有边际，要不断学习。

examples.zh: 学海无涯，我们要活到老学到老。
examples.en: The sea of learning has no shore, so we should keep learning all our lives.

examples.zh: 学海无涯苦作舟，只有努力才能前进。
examples.en: The sea of learning is boundless and hard work is the boat; only effort gets you across.

examples.zh: 读了博士才知道，学海无涯。
examples.en: Only after doing a doctorate did I realise that learning has no end.

usage.en: Encouraging; commonly seen on school walls and in graduation messages. Usually a stand-alone maxim.
usage.zh: 勉励语，常见于校园标语、毕业赠言。多单独作格言用。

natural: as incompatible as water and fire

meaning.en: Two sides hopelessly opposed and unable to coexist.
meaning.zh: 像水和火一样互不相容，形容双方对立到不能并存。

examples.zh: 两家公司在市场上势如水火。
examples.en: The two companies are bitter rivals in the market.

examples.zh: 他们俩一见面就势如水火，吵个不停。
examples.en: Whenever those two meet they're at daggers drawn and keep quarrelling.

examples.zh: 两派观点势如水火，难以调和。
examples.en: The two schools of thought are irreconcilable.

usage.en: Describes bitter opposition between groups or people. Predicate; often 势同水火.
usage.zh: 形容双方尖锐对立。作谓语；也说“势同水火”。

meaning.en: To save and prepare in good times against hard times.
meaning.zh: 平时储存粮食，防备荒年；比喻事先做好准备。

equivalents: lay in stores against lean times

examples.zh: 家里存了点钱，也是积谷防饥。
examples.en: We have put a little money by, just as a precaution against hard times.

examples.zh: 老一辈人讲究积谷防饥，粮食从不浪费。
examples.en: The older generation believed in storing up grain and never wasted food.

examples.zh: 买份保险就是积谷防饥，以防万一。
examples.en: Buying insurance is saving for a rainy day, just in case.

usage.en: Prudent advice; usually in the pair 养儿防老，积谷防饥. Predicate or maxim.
usage.zh: 劝人未雨绸缪；常与“养儿防老”连用。作谓语或格言。

natural: take the effect for the cause

meaning.en: To mistake effect for cause; to get the logic of cause and effect backwards.
meaning.zh: 把结果当成原因，因果颠倒。

equivalents: put the cart before the horse

examples.zh: 说富人因为聪明而富，是倒果为因。
examples.en: To say rich people are rich because they're clever is to get cause and effect backwards.

examples.zh: 他不是因为失败而失望，而是因为失望才失败，别倒果为因。
examples.en: He doesn't lose heart because he failed; he failed because he lost heart, so don't reverse the logic.

examples.zh: 分析问题要防止倒果为因。
examples.en: In analysing a problem, guard against confusing effect with cause.

usage.en: Used in analysis, argument and commentary to point out faulty reasoning. Predicate.
usage.zh: 用于分析、论辩，指出因果颠倒的逻辑错误。作谓语。

meaning.en: To answer a wrong with fairness and justice, neither with revenge nor with sentimental kindness.
meaning.zh: 用公正、正直的态度对待怨恨，不报复也不一味宽容。

examples.zh: 对待伤害过他的人，他以直报怨，既不报复也不假装没事。
examples.en: Towards those who had wronged him he responded with fairness, neither retaliating nor pretending nothing had happened.

examples.zh: 以直报怨，以德报德，这是孔子的主张。
examples.en: Meeting grievance with uprightness and kindness with kindness was Confucius's view.

examples.zh: 面对不公，我们要以直报怨，依法维权。
examples.en: Faced with injustice we answer with justice and defend our rights by law.

story.en: Someone asked, 'What about repaying grudges with kindness?' Confucius replied: 'Then with what would you repay kindness? Repay grievance with uprightness, and kindness with kindness' (以直报怨，以德报德).
story.zh: 有人问“以德报怨，何如？”孔子说：“何以报德？以直报怨，以德报德。”

usage.en: Often contrasted with 以德报怨 (repaying evil with kindness). Respectful; used in ethical discussion.
usage.zh: 常与“以德报怨”对举。含敬意，多用于谈道德。

literal: say · each person · each person · differ

meaning.en: Everyone has a different opinion on the matter.
meaning.zh: 每个人说法各不相同，意见不一。

equivalents: every man to his own view

examples.zh: 对这起事故的原因，专家们言人人殊。
examples.en: Experts have widely differing views on the cause of the accident.

examples.zh: 关于作者的生平，史书言人人殊。
examples.en: On the author's life, the histories all tell different stories.

examples.zh: 评价一部电影，往往言人人殊。
examples.en: People nearly always have different opinions of a film.

usage.en: Formal; 殊 means 'different'. Describes disagreement without hostility. Predicate.
usage.zh: 较书面；“殊”意为不同。形容意见分歧，不含敌意。作谓语。

meaning.en: A person of high skill is bold and unafraid.
meaning.zh: 本领高强的人胆子也大。

examples.zh: 他艺高胆大，一个人就敢闯那片原始森林。
examples.en: Being so skilled he's bold enough to enter that primeval forest alone.

examples.zh: 老消防员艺高胆大，冲在最前面。
examples.en: The veteran firefighter, skilled and fearless, charged to the front.

examples.zh: 艺高胆大是好事，但也不能轻敌。
examples.en: Being skilled and bold is good, but don't underestimate the enemy.

usage.en: Usually praise; also used in the saying 艺高人胆大. Can warn against overconfidence. Predicate.
usage.zh: 多含赞扬；也说“艺高人胆大”。有时提醒不要轻敌。作谓语。

meaning.en: To regard oneself as nobler and purer than others; to be self-righteously aloof.
meaning.zh: 自以为品格高尚，看不起别人。

examples.zh: 他自命清高，不愿和同事来往。
examples.en: He thinks himself above it all and won't mix with his colleagues.

examples.zh: 别自命清高了，你也要吃饭。
examples.en: Stop acting so holier-than-thou; you need to eat too.

examples.zh: 她那种自命清高的态度，让人很反感。
examples.en: Her self-righteous aloofness puts people off.

usage.en: Derogatory; the person's claim to purity is mocked. Predicate or attributive.
usage.zh: 贬义，嘲讽对方自以为清高。可作谓语、定语。

literal: one after another · follow · become · custom
natural: handed down until it becomes custom

meaning.en: Something handed down over time until it becomes an established custom.
meaning.zh: 长期沿袭下来，变成习惯或风俗。

examples.zh: 这个节日的做法相沿成习，已有几百年。
examples.en: The way of keeping this festival has become custom over several centuries.

examples.zh: 过年放鞭炮，相沿成习。
examples.en: Setting off firecrackers at New Year has become an established custom.

examples.zh: 公司里的一些规矩相沿成习，没人知道原因。
examples.en: Some rules in the company have become custom and nobody knows why.

usage.en: Neutral; can describe good traditions or just habits. Formal register. Predicate.
usage.zh: 中性，可指好传统，也可指一般习惯。书面语。作谓语。

pinyin: rén wèi cái sǐ, niǎo wèi shí wáng
literal: people · for · wealth · die, birds · for · food · perish
natural: men die for wealth, birds for food

meaning.en: People will risk, even lose, their lives chasing money, just as birds die for food.
meaning.zh: 人为了钱财可以拼命甚至丧命，就像鸟为了觅食送命一样。

equivalents: men die for gold as birds for grain

examples.zh: 人为财死，鸟为食亡，贪心的人没有好下场。
examples.en: Men die for wealth, birds for food; greedy people come to no good end.

examples.zh: 他明知有风险还是去赌，真是人为财死。
examples.en: He gambled though he knew the risk; truly a man dying for money.

examples.zh: 别说“鸟为食亡”，钱重要，命更重要。
examples.en: Don't say 'birds die for food'; money matters but life matters more.

usage.en: Folk saying, half-resigned, half-critical. It can excuse greed, so use with care. Either half can be used alone.
usage.zh: 民间俗语，带无奈和批评。可能被用来为贪婪开脱，需慎用。上下句可单用。

meaning.en: Plump and well-fed in a coarse way; round-faced and heavy-set.
meaning.zh: 头大、脸胖，形容人胖而富态，常含贬义。

examples.zh: 那个肥头大耳的老板一看就是个暴发户。
examples.en: That fat-faced boss looked at a glance like a nouveau riche.

examples.zh: 他长得肥头大耳，却很和善。
examples.en: He is round-faced and heavy, but quite gentle.

examples.zh: 电影里的反派总是肥头大耳的形象。
examples.en: The film villain is always portrayed as a fat, jowly man.

usage.en: Describes looks; usually derogatory or teasing, and rude about real people. Attributive.
usage.zh: 描写外貌，多含贬义或调侃，对真人说较失礼。作定语。

natural: tear down in the east to mend in the west

meaning.en: To rob Peter to pay Paul; to solve one problem by creating another, especially with money.
meaning.zh: 拆掉东边来补西边，比喻勉强应付，用甲补乙，多指借钱周转。

examples.zh: 他靠借新债还旧债，拆东补西地维持公司。
examples.en: He kept the firm going by borrowing new loans to repay old ones, robbing Peter to pay Paul.

examples.zh: 日子过得紧巴巴，只能拆东补西。
examples.en: Money is tight and we can only juggle debts.

examples.zh: 工程款拆东补西，迟早要出问题。
examples.en: Shuffling the project funds around like that will cause trouble sooner or later.

usage.en: Describes a stopgap that is not a solution; often about debts. Predicate or adverbial.
usage.zh: 形容临时补救并非真正解决；常指债务。作谓语、状语。

natural: do it personally and put it into practice

meaning.en: To carry out something in person and put theory into practice.
meaning.zh: 亲自去做，亲身实践。

examples.zh: 学习中医要躬行实践，光看书是不够的。
examples.en: To learn traditional medicine you must practise in person; books alone aren't enough.

examples.zh: 他躬行实践自己的环保主张。
examples.en: He puts his environmental beliefs into practice himself.

examples.zh: 干部应躬行实践，不能只发号施令。
examples.en: Officials should do things personally, not just give orders.

usage.en: Praise; formal, used in speeches and advice. Also 身体力行 in everyday speech.
usage.zh: 褒义，较书面，用于讲话和劝勉。口语中更常说“身体力行”。

meaning.en: 'By the grace of Heaven and the mandate it gives': the stock opening of an imperial edict.
meaning.zh: “遵奉天命，承受国运”，古代皇帝诏书开头的套语。

examples.zh: 古装剧里，太监常念：“奉天承运，皇帝诏曰……”
examples.en: In period dramas the eunuch often chants: 'By Heaven's mandate the Emperor decrees...'

examples.zh: 奉天承运的说法，体现了君权神授。
examples.en: The phrase 'by Heaven's mandate' reflects the divine right of kings.

examples.zh: 他模仿圣旨的口气，念了句“奉天承运”。
examples.en: Mimicking the tone of an imperial edict, he intoned 'By Heaven's mandate'.

usage.en: Used almost only in historical contexts, or jokingly in imitation of decrees. Full formula: 奉天承运皇帝诏曰.
usage.zh: 基本只用于历史语境，或戏仿圣旨。完整套语为“奉天承运皇帝诏曰”。

meaning.en: To hold much the same view as someone else.
meaning.zh: 看法大致相同。

examples.zh: 你也觉得这个方案好？英雄所见略同！
examples.en: You think the plan is good too? Great minds think alike!

examples.zh: 我们对这件事所见略同。
examples.en: We largely agree on this matter.

examples.zh: 两位专家所见略同，都建议手术。
examples.en: The two specialists reached much the same view and both advised surgery.

usage.en: Friendly and complimentary; often in 英雄所见略同 (a compliment to oneself and the other). Predicate.
usage.zh: 友好、略带夸赞；常说“英雄所见略同”。作谓语。

meaning.en: The reality falls short of the reputation; often used modestly of oneself.
meaning.zh: 实际难以和名声相符；常用作谦辞。

equivalents: fail to live up to one's name
not as good as the reputation

examples.zh: 盛名之下，其实难副，我只怕辜负大家的期望。
examples.en: Under so great a reputation I can hardly live up to it, and fear I'll let you all down.

examples.zh: 这家网红店名气很大，却其实难副。
examples.en: This viral restaurant is famous but doesn't live up to its name.

examples.zh: 过奖了，其实难副，惭愧惭愧。
examples.en: You flatter me; I'm not what you say, and I'm embarrassed.

story.en: Li Gu wrote to Huang Qiong, warning that a man of great fame has trouble living up to it: 'Under a lofty reputation, the reality is hard to match' (盛名之下，其实难副).
story.zh: 李固写信劝黄琼：“盛名之下，其实难副。”

usage.en: Mostly in the phrase 盛名之下，其实难副; as self-deprecation or as criticism. Literary.
usage.zh: 多见于“盛名之下，其实难副”；可作自谦，也可作批评。书面语。

natural: your honoured surname and great name

meaning.en: A polite way of asking someone's name: 'may I know your name?'
meaning.zh: 敬辞，询问对方姓名。

equivalents: may I ask your esteemed name

examples.zh: 请问先生尊姓大名？
examples.en: May I ask your esteemed name, sir?

examples.zh: 这位老前辈尊姓大名，晚辈好上门拜访。
examples.en: May I know the senior's honoured name so I can call on you?

examples.zh: 他故意装出一副文绉绉的样子，问：“尊姓大名？”
examples.en: He put on a scholarly air and asked, 'Your esteemed name?'

usage.en: Old-fashioned polite question, now mostly in period dramas or jokes. Never use it of yourself (use 免贵姓…).
usage.zh: 旧式客套话，现多见于古装剧或玩笑。不能用于自己（自称用“免贵姓……”）。

natural: no room to put a word in

meaning.en: Nothing to say about it; no room for criticism or interference.
meaning.zh: 没有插嘴或评论的余地。

examples.zh: 这是他们的家事，外人无可置喙。
examples.en: It's their family business, and outsiders have no say.

examples.zh: 他的专业水平极高，我们无可置喙。
examples.en: His expertise is so high that we have nothing to say.

examples.zh: 事实俱在，对方无可置喙。
examples.en: The facts are all there and the other side can say nothing.

usage.en: Often with 外人/旁人 as subject. Formal. 喙 (huì) is a beak, i.e. a mouth, here used figuratively.
usage.zh: 常以外人、旁人作主语。较书面。“喙”本指鸟嘴，这里比喻人的嘴。

natural: throw a fit and roll on the ground

meaning.en: To throw a tantrum, behaving like a shameless brat to get one's way.
meaning.zh: 大吵大闹，在地上打滚，耍无赖。

examples.zh: 孩子在商场撒泼打滚要玩具，家长很尴尬。
examples.en: The child threw a tantrum in the mall for a toy, and the parent was embarrassed.

examples.zh: 她一不顺心就撒泼打滚，大家都怕了她。
examples.en: She throws a fit whenever she doesn't get her way, and everyone is afraid of her.

examples.zh: 他撒泼打滚也没用，规定就是规定。
examples.en: Throwing a tantrum won't help him; the rule is the rule.

usage.en: Derogatory, colloquial. 撒 is read sā in this word.
usage.zh: 贬义，口语。“撒”读sā。

meaning.en: True military strength is to stop war; the Chinese character 武 is built from 止 (stop) and 戈 (weapon).
meaning.zh: 真正的武力在于制止战争；“武”字由“止”和“戈”组成。

equivalents: true strength lies in stopping war
the martial art is to end fighting

examples.zh: 止戈为武，我们的军队是为了和平而存在。
examples.en: Stopping the spear is martial prowess: our army exists for peace.

examples.zh: 老教练常说，止戈为武，真正的高手不轻易出手。
examples.en: The old coach often says that true martial skill lies in not fighting; real masters seldom strike.

examples.zh: 止戈为武，这个字形里藏着古人的和平观。
examples.en: The shape of 武 holds the ancients' view of peace.

story.en: After the battle of Bi, King Zhuang of Chu said: 'In the character 武, 止 (stop) is combined with 戈 (spear): to stop the spear is martial' (夫文，止戈为武).
story.zh: 楚庄王说：“夫文，止戈为武。”

usage.en: A principle about peace, with a folk-etymology flavour (modern scholars read 止 as 'foot', not 'stop'). Formal.
usage.zh: 表达和平理念，带字形释义的色彩（今人多认为“止”本义为脚）。较书面。

meaning.en: Of branches, growing out sideways at angles; figuratively, writing that digresses or has varied extra detail.
meaning.zh: 枝条向旁边斜着生长；也比喻文章在主线之外另有枝节。

examples.zh: 老梅树旁逸斜出，别有风致。
examples.en: The old plum tree sends its branches out aslant, with a charm of its own.

examples.zh: 这篇散文旁逸斜出，读来趣味盎然。
examples.en: The essay wanders off the main line so pleasantly that it is a joy to read.

examples.zh: 盆景要修剪，不能让枝条旁逸斜出。
examples.en: Bonsai should be pruned, and the branches not allowed to sprawl.

usage.en: Literary; literal use for plants, figurative for prose. Can be neutral or mildly negative if the digression is aimless.
usage.zh: 书面语；本义用于植物，比喻义用于文章。可中性，若离题则略含贬义。
